cards.text: Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, just asked whether Jesus' parable about servants staying ready was for the disciples or for everyone (Luke 12:41). Jesus answered with more about servants and their master (Luke 12:42-48). Now He says He has come to ignite a fire on the earth.

cards.question: Jesus says He came to ignite a fire on the earth. How does He feel about that fire?

answers.text: He wishes it were burning already
He wishes it could wait a while
He wishes it would go out soon

cards.text: But Jesus also has something He has to go through. He calls it a baptism He has to undergo.

cards.question: Jesus says He has a baptism to undergo, and He feels calm and settled until it is accomplished.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, "Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth?" And friend, His answer is no.

cards.question: Jesus says He hasn't come to bring peace to the earth. What does He say He brings instead?

cards.text: Then Jesus brings it right into the house: from now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three. That's not a family meeting anymore, friend, that's a VOTE.

cards.question: Jesus says the division will come even between fathers and sons.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to the crowds and talks about the one thing EVERYBODY checks: the weather. He starts with a cloud rising in the west.

cards.question: When the crowds see a cloud rising in the west, what do they say is coming?

cards.text: And that is what happens: they just look up, call it, and they're RIGHT. I can't even tell when a batch is done without opening the oven nine times.

cards.question: When the south wind blows, the crowds say it will be ___.

cards.text: And sure enough, it's hot. Then Jesus calls them hypocrites, people who know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky.

cards.question: The crowds can read the earth and sky. But Jesus asks why they can't interpret something else. What is it?
Jesus tells the crowds to let someone else decide for them what is right.

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: you and your adversary, on your way to the magistrate together. And He warns that it might not end well for you.

cards.question: On the way to the magistrate, Jesus says to make every effort to ___ with your adversary, or it might not end well.

cards.text: Otherwise, your adversary may drag you off to the judge, the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison. One handoff after another, like the world's WORST relay race.

cards.question: Jesus says that if the officer throws you into prison, you'll get out before you've paid the very last penny.
